Prevention: Plant at or thin out cocoa trees to recommended spacing of 3m x 3m
Reduce humidity on the farm by weeding farm frequently (3-4 times/year), reduce overhead shade, prune trees judiciously in
Avoid wounding the trunk during farm operations (eg. weeding and harvesting)
Remove infected pod immediately to prevent infection spreading onto the stem and branches through the peduncle (pod stalk)
Monitoring: Monitor cocoa trees for symptoms of canker on trunk and branches on regular basis especially during the rainy season
Look for diseased, discoloured areas on the trunk and branches with red/brown ooze or gummosis.
Once the bark is removed the lesion with have a red/brown colour
P. megakarya infection areas look for canker symptoms mainly on lower parts of the cocoa tree trunk at the beginning of the black pod season (when rains have started).
This is because the disease mainly lives in the soil
P. palmivora areas, look out for canker symptom on whole trunk and branches higher in the cocoa tree as infection can occur from the flower cushions
Direct Control: Scrape the surface of canker with a sharp machette to expose the lesions on the wood and let them dry out
The scraped exposed may be sprayed or painted with
Restrictions: When using a pesticide or botanical, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label
Do not use chemicals with the same mode of action year after year as this can lead to resistance
